primary_sources: Google MLOps Continuous Delivery & Architecture Framework

rules.explanation: Saving unversioned models or using unsafe serialization formats makes deployment brittle and exposes security risks.
rules.do: Serialize models using standardized formats (e.g., ONNX, SafeTensors, joblib) and track model versions explicitly.
rules.dont: Do not rely on unsafe raw pickle files for untrusted production inference or overwrite model files without version tags.

rules.explanation: Machine learning models must be wrapped in lightweight, high-performance web frameworks to serve inference requests reliably.
rules.do: Expose models via production-ready microservice endpoints (e.g., FastAPI, TorchServe, Triton) with input schema validation.
rules.dont: Do not execute model inference directly inside blocking desktop GUI threads or unvalidated raw HTTP request handlers.

rules.explanation: Without tracking training runs, metrics, and parameters, ML experiments cannot be audited or reliably reproduced.
rules.do: Integrate experiment tracking tools (e.g., MLflow, Weights & Biases, DVC) to log hyperparameter runs, dataset versions, and artifacts.
rules.dont: Do not track experiment metrics manually in unversioned text logs or spreadsheet files.

rules.rule_name: Data Drift and Model Performance Monitoring
rules.explanation: Real-world data distribution changes over time (concept drift/data drift), leading to silent degradation of model accuracy in production.
rules.do: Implement monitoring mechanisms (e.g., Evidently AI, Prometheus) to detect feature distribution shifts and trigger retraining alerts.
rules.dont: Do not deploy models into production without monitoring live inference latency, throughput, and distribution drift.
